newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields fall, crown firms vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields fall, crown firms vs dollar.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended somewhat lower on Tuesday, supported by a stronger U.S. debt market, while the crown firmed against the dollar and softened against the mark.
"U.S. yields could easily come down quite a bit more and initially they could pull Europe along. In the longterm it's somewhat more uncertain (if Europe will follow suit)," a trader said.
The six-month T-bill rate fell two basis points to 4.29 percent while the 10-year bond yield slipped one basis point to 6.44 percent.
The crown firmed to 7.9043 against the dollar from 7.9523 late on Monday but softened to 4.3220 against the mark from 4.3055.
"People are buying marks against virtually everything. Many players have been long in dollars and pounds and what we see is profit taking," a trader said.
"I think the crown might soften to 4.34 against the mark," he said.
